extracted.intended_audience: general readers seeking practical-philosophical guidance on character and living
extracted.subtask_description: An essayistic set of practical and philosophical maxims about living well, cultivating character, and practicing creative work—advice to individuals about how to act, think, and persist in the present. The text offers criteria for what constitutes wise conduct, character, and productive habit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fill the hour (present-centered happiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: To fill the hour, and leave no crevice for a repentance or an approval; that is happiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Live in and respect the present hour; enjoy what you find without question. Avoid over-intellectualizing life; 'the true art of life is to skate well on' surfaces. Five minutes of today are worth as much as five minutes in the next millennium; husband the moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finish the moment / find the journey's end in every step
rubrics_metrics.description: To finish the moment, to find the journey's end in every step of the road.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat each moment as complete and sufficient. Do not postpone or defer living to some distant event; do broad justice where you are and 'let us be poised, and wise, and our own, today.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance power and form
rubrics_metrics.description: Human life is made up of the two elements, power and form, and the proportion must be invariably kept if we would have it sweet and sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid excess of either element—each quality in excess becomes harmful. Cultivate a temperate mixture so neither power nor form overwhelms the other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect to the present hour as ballast
rubrics_metrics.description: The only ballast I know is a respect to the present hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In moments of distraction or vertigo from shows and politics, ground yourself in the present. Spontaneity and immediate attention produce good conversation, manners, and action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not postpone your private work
rubrics_metrics.description: Whilst public debates continue, 'thou, dearest scholar, stick to thy foolish task, add a line every hour.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when larger political, legal, or social questions are unsettled, continue your personal labors. Practical controversies are reasons not to delay doing your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value common/public goods ('everything good is on the highway')
rubrics_metrics.description: In popular experience everything good is on the highway; the greatest works are accessible to the common eye.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not fetishize rarity or exclusivity. Public, widely available sources of greatness (nature, canonical books, public galleries) contain the true goods; virtue and beauty are not confined to secluded nooks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace surprise and spontaneity (avoid over-design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Life is a series of surprises, and we thrive by casualties; nature hates calculators; the art of life has a pudency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely less on rigid calculation or excessive planning. Many chief experiences come by fits and starts; too much design in action can stifle genuine power and genius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not over-interpret immediate results; accept uncalculated outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The results of life are uncalculated and uncalculable; the individual is always mistaken about precise outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect unforeseen results from collective endeavors. Accept that personal designs and plans will often yield something different but valuable; the true effect may be deep and secular rather than immediate.

rubrics_metrics.name: The sentiment of origin determines moral dignity
rubrics_metrics.description: The sentiment from which an act sprang determines the dignity of any deed; the question is not what you have done, but at whose command you have done it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate actions by the motive and commanding sentiment behind them, not merely by consequences or appearance. The agent’s inner orientation matters for moral assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate self-trust and know your own facts
rubrics_metrics.description: That need makes in morals the capital virtue of self-trust. It is a main lesson of wisdom to know your own from another's.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not adopt other people's facts or lives; hold to your own axis. Strong self-recovery after distractions helps maintain individuality and truthful action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit excessive sympathy and over-compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A sympathetic person is placed in the dilemma of a swimmer among drowning men, who all catch at him, and if he give so much as a leg or a finger they will drown him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of being overwhelmed by others' needs or moods. Excessive listening and compliance can remove your power to be greatly useful; maintain preoccupied attention to your own aim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preoccupied attention to an aim (focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: A man should not be able to look other than directly and forthright. A preoccupied attention is the only answer to the importunate frivolity of other people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate attention so that others' demands become frivolous in the face of your purpose. Attention tied to a clear aim deflects distraction and preserves effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character as latent reserved force (presence over deeds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Character ... is a reserved force which acts directly by presence, and without means. The largest part of their power was latent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge or cultivate character by presence and a steadiness of being rather than only by enumerated deeds. Character influences environments and inspires trust even without overt action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let action speak; refuse to over-explain
rubrics_metrics.description: All just persons are satisfied with their own praise. They refuse to explain themselves, and are content that new actions should do them that office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid defensive explanation; allow future actions to reveal your nature. Self-exposition is inferior to the demonstration of conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain solitude and self-possession
rubrics_metrics.description: Such men are often solitary, or if they chance to be social, do not need society but can entertain themselves very well alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solitude and the capacity for self-entertainment are signs of inner force. Cultivate independence from public approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer knowing (intellectual life) when genuine
rubrics_metrics.description: People disparage knowing and the intellectual life, and urge doing. I am very content with knowing, if only I could know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value pure intellectual insight even when not immediately practical. A deep knowledge or insight can justify the expense of life’s ordinary cares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept subjectivity of perception
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature and literature are subjective phenomena; every evil and every good thing is a shadow which we cast. 'As I am, so I see.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that perception colors the world; objects become 'our' objects. This calls for humility about apparent facts and vigilance about projection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid infection by others' consciences and fashions
rubrics_metrics.description: We must not harbor such disconsolate consciences, borrowed too from the consciences of other nations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not import another group's anxious prohibitions or fashions. Maintain an autonomous sense of right action grounded in your present strength and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate the mid-world (temperate zone)
rubrics_metrics.description: The middle region of our being is the temperate zone. Between extremes of pure geometry and sensation is the equator of life, of thought, of spirit, of poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid extremes of detached abstract thought and raw sensation. Seek a balanced, practical, and poetic center for a healthy life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do broad justice to companions and circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Let us treat the men and women well; treat them as if they were real; perhaps they are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept and act justly toward the people around you, however humble or odious. Their contentment can be 'the last victory of justice' and more satisfying than poetic sympathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work steadily despite public controversy
rubrics_metrics.description: Whilst the debate goes forward ... stick to thy foolish task, add a line every hour, and between whiles add a line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when legal, political, or social questions remain unsettled, keep producing. Public disputes are not a sufficient excuse to halt private creative labor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greatness is displayed in tendency and direction
rubrics_metrics.description: Most of life seems to be mere advertisement of faculty; our greatness is always in a tendency or direction, not in an action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess or cultivate greatness by consistent inclination and direction over time rather than single spectacular acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work without seeking immediate practical effect
rubrics_metrics.description: That hankering after an overt or practical effect seems to me an apostasy. I am very content with knowing, if only I could know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist the desire for instant measurable impact; intellectual and artistic labors may be valuable in themselves and produce long-term, secular effects.
